summary.intent: Research the current plugin/harness landscape (Claude Code, AGY, Codex, opencode, OpenRouter, Augment, etc.), including using Qwen/Kimi/GLM under Claude Code, and publish it as a high-quality, scannable report artifact that looks excellent on desktop and mobile.
summary.outcome: Published a 7-section, light-theme report artifact at a single stable URL, built from two research workflows, with a verified Playwright+PIL rendering pipeline. Fixed diagram clipping, callout overuse, topnav contrast, table and nav scroll affordances, and diagram scaling across 390–1440px widths.

repo: The main artifact is a single HTML file, coding-agent-landscape.html, in the session scratchpad. Every edit is republished to the same artifact URL rather than creating a new artifact.

Inline SVG diagrams must use `max-width:100%; height:auto` plus explicit width/height attributes matching the viewBox. `width:100%` with `overflow-x:auto` silently clips content behind an invisible macOS overlay scrollbar.
SVG `rx` can be set via CSS (`figure.diagram svg rect { rx: 7px; }`) to round every diagram rect in one line.
Design restraint is required: callouts are only for genuine warnings (4 remain), notes are plain text, and multi-column grids are only for light content. Dense cards stay single-column.

Anthropic ToS bans reusing a Claude Max/Pro subscription outside Claude Code (opencode issue #6930), and claude-code-router cannot pass through OAuth subscriptions. The viable cost architecture is two separate Claude Code lanes (subscription vs ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to cheap models), coordinated externally.
workflow: Verify layout claims by rendering with Playwright and tiling full-page PNGs with PIL, rather than reasoning about CSS blind. This was forced by repeated user frustration with unverified fixes.
Playwright `fullPage` screenshots duplicate position:sticky/fixed elements, producing false-positive bugs. Confirm with a DOM element count plus a scroll-to-element viewport screenshot.
Sweep viewport widths (390/768/1440 and more) with scripted measurements. Tablet widths and undiscoverable-overflow bugs (tables, nav pills, diagrams) only showed up this way.
A forked subagent returned with 0 tool calls. Relaunch as general-purpose with an explicit instruction to use WebSearch/WebFetch.
Fact-check stats before they go in the report. A '65% reasoning failures' stat did not exist in the cited paper and was replaced with the verified figures.

friction: Repeated user frustration with unverified design claims (clipped diagram text, tiny fonts, callout overload, crammed columns), which led to strongly worded feedback.
Piecemeal edits were criticized, and the user wanted holistic report-wide updates.
The Playwright fullPage sticky-element artifact looked like a real topnav duplication bug and took extra investigation to disprove.
The initial diagram fix (bumping font sizes) missed the real root cause, the width:100% scaling and hidden overflow.
Multiple hidden-overflow bugs of the same class (diagrams, tables, nav pills) were found one at a time rather than all at once.
open_items: The user's question about the sticky pill nav vs a hamburger was answered (keep the pills), but this was not tested on real devices.
Stripe's OpenRouter acquisition is pending and should be re-checked once it closes.
The report is mostly verified by headless Chromium only; real-device and Safari rendering were not checked.
Some community-sourced claims in the report (e.g. skill counts, ToxicSkills 36%) were rated 'likely' rather than confirmed.
